note: Signatures, error namespaces, models, auth and DI. These are the claims that decide whether code an agent writes from the skill compiles and behaves — the signature and namespace ones especially, because they are what a positional call and a catch ladder are built from.

assertions.claim: Every generated operation ends `RequestOptions? requestOptions = null, CancellationToken ct = default`, in that order.
RequestOptions has exactly one property, LogLevel?.
assertions.defends: dotnet-calling-endpoints § requestOptions bullet; dotnet-configuration-resilience § per-call override

assertions.claim: SdkException<T> lives in {RootNamespace}.Core.Exceptions.
SdkException<TError> has no `where TError : ApiError` constraint — which is why TError can be a RawError, and why catching a real-but-wrong error type compiles and then never fires.
assertions.defends: dotnet-error-handling § two shapes and § 'Guessing wrong is only sometimes a compile-time error'

assertions.claim: ApiError (and RawError) live in {RootNamespace}.Core.ErrorResponse, NOT with SdkException.

A typed {Operation}Error's body type comes from {RootNamespace}.Models — the fourth using a Case A catch needs once it names the body's type. Floor of 1: this pins the SHAPE where the construct is emitted at all. A legitimate SDK whose definition never produces one cannot settle it — the empty-glob rule turns that into a SKIP, not a failure.

No model property carries a [JsonConverter], so a DateTimeOffset property round-trips as System.Text.Json's default ISO-8601-with-offset. The four date converters exist but attach to whole-response payloads.
Four date converters are generated: ISO-8601, RFC-1123, Unix epoch, date-only.
[JsonIgnore(WhenWritingNull)] is emitted only on optional properties with no initializer; a defaulted one is always serialized.
The DataAnnotations attributes the generator emits are never evaluated by the SDK — they document the provider's contract, they do not guard the call.
assertions.defends: dotnet-models § Validation attributes are documentation, not enforcement

assertions.claim: Generated enums are `public sealed record`s — which is WHY ToString() returns the record debug form rather than the wire value.
String-enum known values are indexed case-insensitively, so FromValue("captured") returns the CAPTURED constant and the declared casing goes on the wire. Int enums match exactly.
TypedEnum DOES override ToString() correctly — the trap is that each generated enum is a record whose synthesised ToString() shadows it. Both halves must hold for the warning to be accurate.
The implicit conversion targets TValue — which is why `+` yields the wire value on a string enum and the debug form on an int enum.
The Optional<T> backing a union is internal — you interact only through the factories and TryGet.
Tokens are reused until 30s before expiry.
When the server omits expires_in, IsExpired short-circuits to false — the token is cached for the client's life and only a 401 replaces it.
assertions.defends: dotnet-authentication § Token caching & refresh, the expires_in warning

assertions.claim: Unset credentials produce a no-op scheme, not an error — the request goes out unauthenticated and the provider returns 401.
assertions.defends: dotnet-authentication § Combined / multiple schemes and § Missing credentials must stop the app from starting

assertions.claim: AuthSchemeAny SKIPS unconfigured schemes rather than trying them, so AuthSchemeException is thrown only when a configured scheme fails — and nothing configured throws nothing.
The token cache is an INSTANCE field on the scheme, which the client constructor builds — so a per-request client refetches a token on every call.
Invalidate() is a bare volatile write and does not take the fetch lock — an in-flight fetch can repopulate the cache. It is a hint, not a barrier.
IOAuth2TokenStrategy is public — the token source is a supported extension point, not an internal detail.
assertions.defends: dotnet-authentication § Supplying your own token source

assertions.claim: The password grant implements the NON-refreshable strategy, so a refresh_token in its response is discarded. Only authorization-code refreshes.
assertions.defends: dotnet-authentication § Token caching & refresh, the 'only the authorization-code grant refreshes' bullet

assertions.claim: The generated DI extension registers the client as a singleton — so IHttpClientFactory handler rotation never reaches it and a DNS change is cached indefinitely.
Add{Api}Client fills LoggerFactory from the container, so SDK request logging is already ON in any host — and the {CLIENT}_LOG environment variable is inert on that path.
assertions.defends: dotnet-configuration-resilience § Logging, the three-state table; dotnet-client-initialization § options class

assertions.claim: The extension resolves the DEFAULT (unnamed) IHttpClientFactory client — which is why a handler attached there has an app-wide blast radius.

The client constructor eagerly builds the resilience pipelines, the logger (reading the {CLIENT}_LOG env var) and the auth schemes — for an OAuth2 SDK the auth scheme IS the token cache, so a per-request client refetches a token on every call.
